subject: Host vs incumbent — p95/p99 fitment: acceptance criteria and test plan
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@veridian.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Host vs incumbent — p95/p99 fitment: acceptance criteria and test plan

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before Ben kicks off testing: 

Summary of what we heard from Veridian on the call:
- Critical paths: customer-facing chat (short-turn completions) and async summarization jobs.
- Current provider: intermittently meets p95 but exhibits p99 spikes around peak traffic.
- Desired targets: stable p95/p99 for E2E (app edge -> model token generated) for small/medium completions.
- Additional constraints: US data residency for request logs during PoC; no model weights leave the region.

Redwood proposed acceptance criteria (please confirm these):
- Latency targets (95th/99th percentiles) for short completions (<=64 tokens): p95 <= 250 ms, p99 <= 450 ms (E2E, measured at app edge).
- First-byte streaming SLO for chunked responses: first-byte p95 <= 150 ms.
- Sustained throughput: 300 concurrent streams (chat-like sessions) and burst to 800 RPS for short completions without exceeding p99 target.
- CPU/GPU utilization: keep mean serving GPU utilization <= 70% during test windows (so we can validate headroom).

Proposed PoC plan (short):
1) Redwood runs a 48-hour side-by-side test: Veridian-provided harness vs Redwood-hosted API using the same traffic profile and origin (we’ll instrument at the app edge).
2) Use the attached traffic profile and test script (veridian_poc_traffic_profile.json, slo_test_script.py).
3) Run three 2-hour steady-state windows and three 30-minute burst windows.
4) Share raw traces and percentiles; both sides validate measurement methodology.

Attachments: veridian_poc_traffic_profile.json (traffic mix), slo_test_script.py (load runner harness), poe-criteria-checklist.md (acceptance checklist).

Next steps / asks: 
- Samantha / Veridian: confirm the acceptance criteria above and the PoC dates (we’re proposing Tue 11/23 — Thu 11/25). Also confirm you can provide a signed test NDA for the logs.
- Ben: can you confirm test harness details and whether you need additional infra from Veridian?
- Marissa: I’ll queue pricing/LOI follow-up after PoC if acceptance is met.

Thanks — keen to get this running.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Host vs incumbent — p95/p99 fitment: acceptance criteria and test plan

Dylan — thanks for the clear summary. We’re aligned on most of this; a few clarifications from our side: 

1) Acceptance criteria: the p95/p99 numbers look reasonable as long as the measurement point is clearly defined — our security team requires that the p99 includes network transit to our edge but excludes downstream client rendering time.
2) Data residency: we can supply logs from our edge in the US and are OK with Redwood collecting anonymized request-level timing for the PoC. We’ll need the NDA in place first.
3) Test windows: 11/23–11/25 works for the team here but we’d prefer the long steady-state window to run on 11/24 UTC daytime to capture peak US traffic.
4) Additional ask: can Redwood provide a short checklist of how you’ll measure tokenization differences and any model-variant fallback behavior? Last PoC we saw different tokenizers add ~10–15 ms variability and that skewed p99 comparisons.

If you can incorporate (4) into the test script or checklist, we’ll sign off and get the NDA routed.

Samantha Holt
Head of Integrations | Veridian Solutions
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@veridian.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Nov 2027 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Host vs incumbent — p95/p99 fitment: acceptance criteria and test plan

Thanks — quick technical note and additions to the plan.

Measurement methodology (short):
- Measurement point: instrument at the app edge (VadEdge) for client->edge request and at Redwood ingress for edge->model RPC. E2E = client->edge + edge->model + model response to edge (we’ll exclude any client rendering).
- Tokenization: we’ll add a tokenization shim in the harness so both sides use the same tokenizer binary for the PoC (attached: poe-criteria-checklist.md includes steps). That should remove the 10–15 ms variability you saw.

Test configuration:
- Models: we’ll use the same model family variants that you run in production (we’ll confirm exact weights via the signed NDA). For safety we’ll pin to the 1.2.x runtime on Redwood.
- Traffic shape: see veridian_poc_traffic_profile.json — includes 70% short chat (<=64 tokens), 20% medium (65–512 tokens), 10% summarization (async).
- Streaming: implement a first-byte timing trace and a chunk timing trace for the first 4 chunks. First-byte SLO target: p95 <= 150 ms.
- Concurrency/throughput: we’ll run the three steady-state windows at ~300 concurrent streams and the burst windows up to 800 RPS for 30 minutes. We’ll record GPU metrics and scheduler queue depth to validate headroom.

Validation and pass/fail:
- Pass = meets p95 & p99 for short completions across the three steady windows AND meets first-byte p95 across streaming tests.
- If p99 misses but p95 is met, we’ll surface the traces and propose a mitigation (routing to variant B or transient capacity bump) and re-run the window; pass requires both percentiles.

Attachments: I’ve updated poe-criteria-checklist.md with the tokenizer shim steps and included markers for where Veridian should inject edge timestamps. I’ve also attached slo_test_script.py (load runner harness) — we’ll share the runner config and telemetry dashboards prior to the window.

Action items assigned:
- Ben: finalize harness and share runbook by EOD Thu 11/18.
- Dylan: route the NDA and confirm PoC schedule with Marissa for pricing hold.
- Samantha: get NDA in motion and confirm the list of model variants you want Redwood to use.

-ben
